maria: heads-up — after the model-onboard merge (checkpoint v3.4.1) staging is showing a huge alloc spike. p50 OK, p99 ~4x baseline. :grimacing:
ashok: repro steps? is this seen on long sequences only or all traffic?
maria: mostly chat workloads. suspect tokenizer length shift? new checkpoint emits extra EOS tokens sometimes -> longer seqs. attaching quick log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T21:02:11Z] request_id=abc123 model=redwood-v3.4.1 seq_len=198 tokens_allocated=3.2GB p99_latency_ms=1287
[2026-03-17T21:02:12Z] request_id=def456 model=redwood-v3.4.1 seq_len=76 tokens_allocated=780MB p99_latency_ms=310
```
maria: note the allocator churn aligns with kernel autoselect switching from fused-attn to fallback path (small-batch kernel) mid-sequence.
ci-bot: perf-ci: nightly/perf-staging failed for p99_latency (threshold exceeded). https://ci/internal/12345 :warning:
ashok: can we bisect commit range for the model onboarding PR? maybe tokenizer config change or the tokenizer packer.
tom: I'll take a quick git-range bisect across the model onboarding commits and the runtime kernel change that landed same day. starting with commits: 8a7f..b3c2
lisa: ran a targeted profiler on staging canary. Captured KV-cache churn + allocator stacks. Looks like longer sequences cause KV cache thrash because our shard-slicing uses token_count per request for placement; higher seqs push requests into a different kernel queue and evict active KV segments. rough flame snippet:
```
Runtime::serve -> KernelSelector::choose -> FallbackKernel::exec -> Alloc::alloc -> KVStore::evict -> Alloc::alloc -> OOM-ish spikes
```
lisa: also found tokenizer patch in model bundle: preserve_eos=true -> padded outputs include EOS at end + additional separator token in some prompts. that increases avg tokens by ~15%.
maria: summary: tokenizer change in bundle + kernel autoselect logic interacting badly -> batch heuristics pick fallback kernels -> higher alloc -> KV thrash -> p99 spike. rollout blocked on staging.
ashok: what's safest short-term? revert model bundle tokenizer config or force kernel selection to prefer fused path when available?
ashok: (cc @tom)
tom: quick mitigation: flip runtime flag to prefer fused kernel for model=redwood-v3.* on staging (runtime flag: kernel_pref=fused). patch ready, testing now.
ops-bot: deploy request by tom queued to canary (deploy/edge-runtime staging).
maria: also created a minimal eval that reproduces behavior in infra tests (incr seq length + repeated separator). adding to regression suite.
lisa: pushed a small tokenizer-diff to the model bundle that reverts preserve_eos change. but that needs model infra approval, longer path.
ci-bot: perf-ci: targeted/regression job queued post-patch.
tom: canary shows p99 back within 1.1x baseline after kernel_pref flip. monitoring for 10m.
maria: thanks. plan: keep kernel_pref override on for staging rollout stop, revert tokenizer change in model bundle for next bundle release, and add gating perf regression test. action items:
- tom: hotfix kernel_pref on staging (done)
- lisa: open model-bundle revert PR + tag for infra audit
- maria: add regression to perf-suite + increase KV eviction logging
- ashok: follow up to evaluate long-term fix in kernel selection heuristics (avoid queue hop on small sequence deltas)

maria: rolling this to rollout-blocked. ping if you see any anomalies. :eyes:
ops-bot: monitor alert: p99_latency returned to baseline at 21:16 UTC.
maria: closing thread, will follow up with postmortem once lisa's revert lands.
